abstract: Detailed biophysical simulations of neuronal networks might help understand brain function. Here, we built a model of mouse barrel cortex focused on its somatotopic map, comprising 33 barrel columns. We investigated dendritic polarity in layer 4 and implemented it in the model, building two circuits differing in a single property of basal dendritic synthesis. In the polarised circuit, layer 4 dendrites were confined to their home barrel; in the symmetric circuit, they were not. We simulated three conditions: i) quiet periods without whisker movement; ii) active free-whisking periods without touch; and iii) active whisking with touch of the C2 whisker. The model exhibited complex spatiotemporal dynamics of neuronal activity across cortical layers, cortical columns, molecularly-defined classes of neurons, and brain states. Using cyclicity analysis, spiking responses were decomposed into activity shared between the two circuits and activity unique to either. Layer 4 dendritic polarisation sharpened the touch response in space and advanced it in time.
